title: fix-round chain: the held root task ends merged when any fix round in its chain merges (luna T-0608 -> T-0607 -> T-0597)
spec:
Evidence (luna-inbox, 2026-10-07): T-0597 (held gate_red) <- fix round T-0607 (fix_round_for T-0597) <- fix round
T-0608 (fix_round_for T-0607, no code change, pinned to wt/T-0607). After the merge at ~05:23 (goal/T-0593 head 19ccbf2,
T-0608 pipeline.merged_at 1791345780), T-0607 had merged_into goal/T-0593 but T-0597 stayed held gate_red, so the goal never
reached close. The Planner set T-0597 done/merged_into by hand at ~09:40. Read luna-inbox/.orchestrator/tasks/T-0597.json,
T-0607.json, T-0608.json and the bus events for them (read only) to find which path left T-0597 held: the walk in
orchestrator/daemon.py:1565-1579 is transitive, so suspect either a later re-gate or hold of T-0597 after the walk (its own
04:39 gate result posted late), or a merge path that does not run that walk (merge_reviewed or the pinned-worktree merge).
Fix the cause so (1) every ancestor in a merged chain ends done/merged_into, and (2) a held task already merged by its chain
is never re-held by a late gate or review result. Put the cause in the commit message.
Tests (tests/test_daemon.py): test_two_level_fix_chain_marks_root_merged, test_late_gate_result_does_not_reheld_merged_root.
Run: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon tests.test_merge. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: the cause is named in the commit message

result.summary:
T-0597 stayed held because T-0607 never recorded which task it was fixing. That's fixed and committed as `907b410` on `task/T-1708`, and `tests.test_daemon` plus `tests.test_merge` pass (271 tests, OK).

**Cause** (also in the commit message): T-0607 was created by hand through `bus_create_task`. Its link to T-0597 was only in its title ("fix round 1 ... for held T-0597"); it had no `constraints.fix_round_for`. When T-0608 merged, `report_merge` followed `constraints.fix_round_for` up the chain. It marked T-0607 merged, found no link on T-0607, and stopped, so T-0597 stayed held `gate_red`. The luna-inbox bus events rule out the other two suspects: nothing re-gated or re-held T-0597 after the merge. Its only later event is the Planner's manual fix at ~09:40.

**Fix** (`orchestrator/daemon.py`):
- **Walking the chain:** a new `_fix_parent()` uses `constraints.fix_round_for` when it is set. Otherwise it reads the task named in a hand-created fix round's title ("fix round ... for held T-xxxx"). It only accepts that task if it is an unmerged execute task in the same goal. `report_merge` uses it to walk the chain, with cycle protection, and marks every ancestor done/`merged_into`. The `accepted_at` stamp on the root works as before.
- **No re-hold after merge:** `stamp()` refuses to set `held` on a task that already has `merged_into`. That covers the gate-red, review-held and spec-review holds. `gate()` also drops a result if the task merged while its gate was running, and the stale_high hold skips merged tasks.

One thing to know: falling back to the title is a heuristic. It only helps when the Planner keeps that title wording, so setting `fix_round_for` on hand-created fix rounds is still the reliable route.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_daemon.py`):
- `test_two_level_fix_chain_marks_root_merged`: rebuilds the luna chain with a hand-created middle round and checks that all three tasks end done/merged. It also checks that a title naming a task in another goal is ignored.
- `test_late_gate_result_does_not_reheld_merged_root`: the chain merges while the root's gate is still running, then the gate comes back red; the root stays done. A late review hold is also refused.

**Files changed:** `orchestrator/daemon.py`, `tests/test_daemon.py`

**Test output (failures only):** none.

The test command ran longer than the 120 s tool limit and was moved to the background automatically. I waited in the foreground for it to finish, so nothing was left running.
